41: The actions of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas and vaiśyas, and of śūdras, scorcher of foes, are divided according to the guṇas that arise from their own nature.
42: Calm, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forbearance and uprightness, knowledge, discernment and faith are the action born of a brāhmaṇa's own nature.
43: Heroism, vigour, firmness, skill, and also not fleeing in battle, giving and the bearing of a lord are the action born of a kṣatriya's own nature.
44: Farming, protecting cows and trade are the action born of a vaiśya's own nature. Action that consists of service is the śūdra's, and it too is born of the śūdra's own nature.
45: Each person, delighting in their own action, attains full perfection. Hear how one who is devoted to their own action finds perfection.
46: A human being finds perfection by worshipping, through their own action, the one from whom beings come forth and by whom all this is pervaded.
47: One's own dharma, even without merit, is better than another's dharma well performed. Doing the action ordained by one's own nature, one incurs no fault.
48: One should not abandon inborn action, son of Kuntī, even if it has fault. For all undertakings are covered by fault, as fire is by smoke.
49: One whose buddhi is unattached everywhere, who has conquered the self and whose longing is gone, reaches through renunciation the supreme perfection of actionlessness.
50: Learn from me, son of Kuntī, only in brief, how one who has attained perfection attains brahman, which is the highest culmination of knowledge.
51: Such a person is joined with a purified buddhi and has restrained the self with firmness, has abandoned sound and the other objects of the senses, and has cast aside attraction and aversion.
52: Such a person dwells in solitude and eats lightly, with speech, body and mind restrained, always intent on the yoga of meditation, having taken refuge in dispassion.
53: Having let go of ego, force, pride, desire, anger and possession, without the sense of mine and at peace, such a person is fit to become brahman.
54: One who has become brahman, the self serene, neither grieves nor longs. The same toward all beings, that person gains supreme devotion to me.
55: By devotion one comes to know me, how great I am and who I am in truth. Then, having known me in truth, one enters immediately after that.
56: Even while always doing all actions, one who has me as refuge reaches by my grace the eternal, imperishable abode.
57: Lay down all actions in me with your mind and hold me as the highest. Resort to the yoga of buddhi and keep your thought constantly on me.
58: With your thought on me, you will cross over all difficulties by my grace. But if out of ego you will not listen, you will perish.
59: If you resort to ego and think that you will not fight, this resolve of yours is in vain. Nature will compel you.
60: You are bound by your own action, son of Kuntī, born of your own nature. What in your delusion you do not wish to do, you will do even against your will.
61: The lord stands in the region of the heart of all beings, Arjuna, and by illusion makes all beings revolve, mounted on a machine.
62: Go to him alone for refuge with your whole being, descendant of Bharata. By his grace you will reach supreme peace, the eternal abode.
63: So I have declared to you knowledge more secret than the secret. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
64: Hear once more my supreme word, the most secret of all. You are firmly beloved to me, and for that reason I will tell you what is good for you.
65: Keep your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow to me. You will come to me alone. Truly I promise you, you are dear to me.
66: Abandon all dharmas and come to me alone for refuge. I will free you from all evils. Do not grieve.
67: You must never speak this to one without austerity, nor to one without devotion, nor to one who does not wish to hear, nor to one who finds fault with me.
68: Whoever declares this supreme secret among my devotees, having shown supreme devotion to me, will come to me alone, without doubt.
69: And no one among humans does what is dearer to me than that person, and no other on earth will be dearer to me than that person.
70: And whoever studies this dialogue of ours, which is in keeping with dharma, would be worshipping me with the sacrifice of knowledge. That is my view.
71: And a person who has faith and finds no fault, and who even just listens, is freed too, and would reach the auspicious worlds of those whose actions are meritorious.
72: Have you heard this, son of Pṛthā, with a one-pointed mind? Has your delusion of ignorance been destroyed, winner of wealth?
73: Delusion is destroyed. By your grace, unfallen one, I have gained memory. I stand firm, my doubt gone. I will do as you say.
74: So I heard this dialogue between the son of Vasudeva and the son of Pṛthā, great in self, a wondrous dialogue that makes the hair stand on end.
75: By the grace of Vyāsa I heard this supreme secret, yoga, directly from Kṛṣṇa, the lord of yoga, as he told it himself.
76: King, as I recall again and again this wondrous, holy dialogue of Keśava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
77: And as I recall again and again that most wondrous form of Hari, my amazement is great, king, and I rejoice again and again.
78: Where Kṛṣṇa, the lord of yoga, is, and where the son of Pṛthā, the bearer of the bow, is, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and firm right conduct. This is my view.
